programs.note: SSA beneficiaries by age (Dec 2024), scaled to Treasury outlays; spouse and survivor benefits only come in three age groups and are spread by population
CMS age shape of Medicare spending (2020, the latest) applied to FY2024 Treasury outlays

CMS age shape of Medicaid spending (2020) applied to the federal portion of Medicaid payments (CMS, calendar 2024). The shape covers federal plus state spending; the federal match differs by group (higher for expansion adults, lower for older people), which this does not capture
VA recipients by age band (FY2024), spread within each band by population, scaled to OMB subfunction 701
OMB subfunction 703 spread like VA compensation recipients by age (no VA health spending by age found)
OMB subfunction 501 spread over ages 5-18 by population

OMB subfunction 502 spread over ages 18-29 by population. It may include student-loan accounting costs (estimates that move with policy), not only cash grants, and no age split of Pell grants or loans was used; treat it as the least certain row
FNS FY2024 SNAP cost spread by SNAP participants by age (FY2023 quality-control sample), assuming equal benefits per person; the 60+ group is spread over ages 60-100 by population

programs.program: School meals, child nutrition and WIC
programs.note: FNS FY2024 child nutrition and WIC costs counted at ages 0-17 (mothers' share of WIC is counted with children)

HUD units times average monthly federal spending (2024), counted at the age of the household head because the file gives no ages for other residents; children in assisted households are not counted as recipients

IRS tax year 2022 credits claimed, put at the likely age of the parent (child age plus mother's age at birth, CDC 2024 births); the childless credit ($2.6B) is spread over ages 25-64 by population. Tax-year dollars, not FY2024 outlays

IRS tax year 2022 nonrefundable child and other dependent credit plus the refundable additional child tax credit, put at the likely age of the parent for children aged 0-16 (child age plus mother's age at birth). Fathers and other claimants are typically a few years older and are not modelled. Tax-year dollars, not FY2024 outlays
